svg.title: Level 2 Enhanced: a monthly operational dashboard
svg.desc: Level 2 Enhanced: a monthly operational dashboard. Stages run across and lanes run down. A monthly operational dashboard, which NHSBSA's Analytical Assurance Decision Tool gives as a worked example of impact 2. Drawn here at Level 2 Enhanced, which is where impact 2 lands at moderate to high likelihood. The route this playbook sets out for work of that kind, not a record of a particular piece of work. Stages, left to right: Engagement and scoping, Design, Analysis, Delivery and sign-off and Review. Commissioner. Owns the question and the resource. Engagement and scoping: State the decision, the deadline and the quality expected. Score the impact with the analyst, and take any disagreement over the level to the Analytical Quality and Assurance Lead. Design: Approve the design before work proceeds, and make sure the reviewer's time is in the schedule. Analysis: Stay available. Review any change of design or method, and resist changing the question late. Delivery and sign-off: See the draft results before sign-off. Confirm it meets your need, apply its limitations, and approve it for release. Review: The review is yours to own, with the analyst. Schedule it annually, or at each reissue if more frequent, and before any reuse for a new purpose. Analyst. Owns the method and the write-up. Engagement and scoping: Clarify the real question and score the impact with your commissioner. Record the decision, the question, what is out of scope and the quality expected. Design: Choose the method, score the likelihood and read your level. Write an assurance plan: who reviews, what and when, with your reviewer named before work starts. Analysis: Profile the input data, including who is missing from it. Do your own checks first, work under version control, and log decisions as they happen. Delivery and sign-off: Write the quality assurance statement, with the caveats in the output itself. Archive the project record, the log and the code together. Review: Record the lessons where the next analyst will look, including what the last run showed could be better. Critical friend. At Level 2 Enhanced, someone who had no hand in producing the work. Design: Confirm the approach answers the question and the assurance planned is right. Put your own time in the schedule. Analysis: Peer review the work and the code, reproducing the calculations from source. Report errors and improvements back, and log what you found. Delivery and sign-off: State the assurance: appropriately scoped, executed, validated, verified and documented. Review: What you reported back is what the next piece of work avoids. None: This lane is empty at Engagement and scoping. Your team lead. Signs the work off, and is named before the work starts. Design: Be named as the approver before the work starts, not found at delivery. Delivery and sign-off: Sign the analysis off, and record your role, the date and what you confirmed in the project record. None: This lane is empty at Engagement and scoping, Analysis and Review. What is handed over. 1: Commissioner to Analyst, at Engagement and scoping. The decision, the deadline and the quality expected. 2: Analyst to Critical friend, at Design. The assurance plan, with the reviewer named on it. 3: Critical friend to Analyst, at Analysis. Findings, which are the analyst's to act on. 4: Analyst to Commissioner, at Delivery and sign-off. Draft results, so they are understood before sign-off. 5: Analyst to Your team lead, at Delivery and sign-off. The output, the quality assurance statement and the project record. 6: Your team lead to Commissioner, at Delivery and sign-off. Signed off by your team lead. Why this one is Level 2 Enhanced: A monthly operational dashboard is impact 2 in NHSBSA's own worked examples, which the tool marks as still to be developed. Impact 2 reads Level 2 Enhanced at moderate and high likelihood, Level 1 Standard at low and Level 3 Comprehensive at very high, so score your own work rather than match it. What Level 2 adds over Level 1 is separation from the work: someone who had no hand in producing it reviews it, named before you start, because a reviewer found afterwards reviews what was produced while one named beforehand shapes it. Your team lead signs it off. The project record, the quality assurance log and the code are archived together and linked from the output. The statement is required but not published until Level 3. Because this one is a regular output it also goes to the review meeting NHSBSA holds every month, chaired by the Analytical Quality and Assurance Lead, which no standard asks for. NHSBSA Producing Quality Analysis Playbook. Service design artefacts for workshop use. Seamus Sands for NHSBSA, SOW-DOC053.

Drawn here at Level 2 Enhanced, which is where impact 2 lands at moderate to high likelihood. The route this playbook sets out for work of that kind, not a record of a particular piece of work.

div.span: 1. Commissioner → Analyst, at Engagement and scoping. The decision, the deadline and the quality expected
2. Analyst → Critical friend, at Design. The assurance plan, with the reviewer named on it
3. Critical friend → Analyst, at Analysis. Findings, which are the analyst's to act on
4. Analyst → Commissioner, at Delivery and sign-off. Draft results, so they are understood before sign-off
5. Analyst → Your team lead, at Delivery and sign-off. The output, the quality assurance statement and the project record
6. Your team lead → Commissioner, at Delivery and sign-off. Signed off by your team lead

div.b: WHY THIS ONE IS LEVEL 2 ENHANCED

div.span: A monthly operational dashboard is impact 2 in NHSBSA's own worked examples, which the tool marks as still to be developed. Impact 2 reads Level 2 Enhanced at moderate and high likelihood, Level 1 Standard at low and Level 3 Comprehensive at very high, so score your own work rather than match it. What Level 2 adds over Level 1 is separation from the work: someone who had no hand in producing it reviews it, named before you start, because a reviewer found afterwards reviews what was produced while one named beforehand shapes it. Your team lead signs it off. The project record, the quality assurance log and the code are archived together and linked from the output. The statement is required but not published until Level 3. Because this one is a regular output it also goes to the review meeting NHSBSA holds every month, chaired by the Analytical Quality and Assurance Lead, which no standard asks for.
